title: Persist daemon plan revisions on submission
description: Objective: deliver the daemon-owned revision producer for stale-plan approval parent task-7265e1fca1984b568a5ec75afba48699. Deliverable: Task.planRevision in packages/moe-daemon/src/types/schema.ts and docs/SCHEMA.md, initialized to 0 for newly created tasks, with absent legacy values interpreted as 0; every successful moe.submit_plan increments the persisted nonnegative safe-integer revision exactly once, including identical resubmissions and all approval modes. Plan and revision must be committed in the same task write before publication; return the persisted revision from submit_plan. Rejected validation and a failed task write must not advance revision/map/events; no wrap, coercion, or reset on reopen. Expected seams: src/state/taskStore.ts, src/tools/submitPlan.ts, and src/tools/submitPlan.test.ts under packages/moe-daemon (5 files including schema/docs). Keep the optional legacy-compatible TypeScript shape if needed rather than mechanically rewriting every historical Task fixture. Error handling: malformed existing non-absent revision refuses as INVALID_INPUT, exhaustion as a stable conflict, and task-write failure remains observable. NOT in scope: approval CAS, IDE changes, changing auto-approval policy, or Wave 1 records. This child establishes the mandatory submit_plan behavior; whether awaiting in-place amendments/DoD edits also bump is still a parent-scope decision and must not be advertised as solved by submit-only stamping. Verification from repository root: npm --prefix packages/moe-daemon test (PowerShell: npm.cmd --prefix packages/moe-daemon test); require nonzero Vitest counts and record old-behavior red proof. Do not build/regenerate foreign generated files.

implementationPlan.description: Implement the single revision authority in schema.ts and taskStore.ts. Add documented optional Task.planRevision:number for legacy fixture/read compatibility; createTask always writes owned revision 0 even with an initial plan or caller-provided revision. In updateTask, strip incoming planRevision, treat undefined top-level implementationPlan/definitionOfDone as omitted, and keep the existing sanitation rules for supplied values. Privately decode current stored revision as undefined=>0 or a nonnegative Number.isSafeInteger number; reject every other value using the existing invalidInput helper without coercion. After sanitation, compare the candidate implementationPlan and definitionOfDone against the corresponding canonical sanitized prior values structurally (array order significant, object key insertion order irrelevant, including all retained step/amendment fields). Derive shouldBump = PLAN_SUBMITTED event OR actual surface change; compute exactly one increment even when both predicates/fields change. Metadata-only updates retain the numeric revision; a legacy row can materialize 0 on its next successful write. Error handling: when a required increment would exceed Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, throw existing MoeError with numeric STATE_CONFLICT, explicit codeName PLAN_REVISION_EXHAUSTED and task/current-revision context before any write. Put the derived stamp into the same fresh Task object and primary writeEntity call as the plan/DoD, keeping write-before-map/activity/event ordering and original IO rejection. Do not mutate the prior task/input, reset on reopen, add caller-specific bumps, or add a parallel persistence/locking abstraction.
implementationPlan.note: schema.ts: added documented optional `Task.planRevision?: number` beside implementationPlan (daemon-owned, creation 0, absent legacy = 0, no migration/schemaVersion bump, non-negative safe-integer domain shared with the clients' Long, caller value stripped). New local helpers: MAX_PLAN_REVISION (Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER); decodeStoredPlanRevision (undefined => 0, else non-negative Number.isSafeInteger or refuse via the existing invalidInput helper with the raw value stringified — no coercion, fails closed on every write, not just submissions); isPlainObject + recursive sameSanitizedSurface (array order significant, object key insertion order irrelevant, every retained key compared so step execution fields and amendment entries participate); derivePlanRevision comparing the sanitized candidate against sanitizeImplementationPlan/sanitizeStringArray of the PRIOR stored values, treating undefined as omitted, and returning current+1 once when the event is PLAN_SUBMITTED or either surface actually changed (both together still +1). Error handling: an exhausted counter throws the existing MoeError with numeric STATE_CONFLICT and explicit codeName PLAN_REVISION_EXHAUSTED plus taskId/currentRevision/maxPlanRevision context, and both refusals happen before any persistence. No caller-specific bump, no reopen reset, no new persistence or locking abstraction, no mutation of the prior task or the caller's input. implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial review of the five-file diff (646 insertions, 2 deletions; no new files). Findings and dispositions:
(1) QUEUED WRITES: derivePlanRevision reads the cached task at the top of updateTask and the write awaits after it, so two updateTask calls that are NOT serialized could both derive N+1 (a lost increment) — the same pre-existing TOCTOU as the assignedWorkerId guard right above it. Every real caller (MCP dispatch, WS handlers) already runs under the global StateManager mutex, and the new test drives two writes through the real state.runExclusive and asserts successive 2 and 3. Deliberately NOT fixed with a new lock: the plan forbids a parallel persistence/locking abstraction. No claim is made that arbitrary unlocked direct updateTask calls are serialized.
(2) SANITIZED-EQUAL ECHO: comparison is sanitized-candidate vs re-sanitized prior, so echoing a legacy row's unsanitized plan back can change the persisted bytes (unknown keys dropped) without a bump. Intended: the versioned thing is the sanitized surface every consumer actually reads. Documented as a sanitized no-op.
(3) EXPLICIT undefined: `implementationPlan: undefined` / `definitionOfDone: undefined` still clears the field on write (pre-existing spread semantics) while counting as omitted for the revision, per the approved plan and its test. Grep confirms no daemon caller passes either as undefined today, so no live path clears a surface without a bump. Flagged for the parent, not silently redefined here.
(4) MALFORMED STAMP FAILS CLOSED ON EVERY WRITE, not only submissions: a corrupted stamp therefore refuses status/metadata writes too, so such a row cannot be repaired through any MCP tool until a human fixes or removes the field (after which it reads as 0 again). That is the specified no-coercion behavior; the alternative would let a bad value survive into a freshness comparison.
(5) NUMERIC DOMAIN: MAX_SAFE_INTEGER+2 collapses to an unsafe double and is refused; exhaustion uses >= so it cannot be stepped over; a metadata-only write at the max still succeeds; MAX-1 advances to MAX.
(6) STRUCTURAL COMPARE: Object.keys + hasOwnProperty (no prototype-chain reads), array order significant, recursion depth bounded by the existing 50-step / 20-amendment / string-length sanitizer caps, so no deep-nesting or huge-input blowup. The surface holds no numbers, so no NaN-inequality trap.
(7) FAILURE PATHS: both refusals throw before writeEntity, so revision, cached task, persisted bytes and the TASK_UPDATED publication are untouched and a retry advances exactly once (tested on submission and on an in-place DoD change). A LATER side effect after a committed plan write — touchWorker, the auto-approval status write, chat posts — can still fail; that does not and must not roll back the committed stamp, and no cross-entity transaction is promised.
(8) CALLER STAMP: stripped from a shallow copy, so the caller's own object is never mutated; forging and resetting are both tested.
(9) OTHER WRITERS: reorderTask, the deleteTask orphan-parent clear and the startup worker purge spread the prior task, so they retain the stamp and never bump; approve/reject/status writes are metadata; amend_plan_step and reopen bump through the store with no tool edits.
(10) TEST HYGIENE: afterEach clears SPEED timers, restores real timers and mocks, and removes the temp project; the SPEED case polls a 10ms real timer with a 5s bound instead of leaving a fake-timer state behind. The two pre-existing strict-type errors in the test file (stale PACE_PER_STEP_MS_DEFAULT import, optional-priority fixture) were left alone — tsconfig excludes *.test.ts, so they are not new and not mine.
(11) SCOPE: only the five declared paths are modified; the temp scratch file used to append the test block was deleted. docs/MCP_SERVER.md is untouched (the CAS sibling owns it), so the returned submit_plan field is documented in docs/SCHEMA.md only. Foreign paths listed in step 1 were never touched; several of them (scripts/moe-agent.*, scripts/tests/mention-provenance.*, one peer task record) have since been committed by their own sessions and are now clean — not by me.
